## This week ...

What a Large Language Model is, and what it is not. We separate the model from the _harness_ that runs it, look at how tool use lets a model check and improve its own output, and compare subscription-based and API-based access. Then we look at R packages that connect R to LLMs, in particular `btw`, which lets a coding agent like Claude Code read R documentation, inspect your data, and run code in your R session.

## Required Reading

These short posts by Hadley Wickham cover the main ideas:

- "[What is an agent?](https://substack.hadley.nz/p/what-is-an-agent)"
- "[Your LLM can't math (and that's ok)](https://substack.hadley.nz/p/your-llm-cant-math-and-thats-ok)"
- "[A coding agent is six functions in a trenchcoat](https://substack.hadley.nz/p/a-coding-agent-is-six-functions-in)"
- "[Auto mode knows it's dangerous (and does it anyway)](https://substack.hadley.nz/p/auto-mode-knows-its-dangerous-and)"

Also look at the documentation for the [`btw`](https://posit-dev.github.io/btw/) and [`ellmer`](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org) packages.
